jobDescription: Aldermoor Bank's payments operations team reconciles card, cheque and faster-payment flows every working day. The Operations Automation Analyst maps manual reconciliation steps, specifies and tests robotic process automation with the automation team, documents controls for operational risk, and moves automations from test into live operation under the bank's automation control framework, reporting on their run results afterwards. The team handles about 3,000 reconciliation breaks a month. Bots are built by a central automation team; the analyst writes the specifications, runs testing with the operations staff and prepares the evidence the control framework asks for.
requirements: Maps manual operations processes and identifies automation candidates.
Specifies and tests robotic process automation in a development environment.
Has moved an automation from test into live operation under a control framework and reported on its run results.
Documents process controls for the operational risk team.
Runs user acceptance testing with operations staff.

evidence.text: Operations Analyst, Fairhaven Building Society (October 2021 to September 2024): mapped the daily suspense-account reconciliation as a swim-lane diagram and timed each manual step over a fortnight, identifying four steps that followed fixed rules.

Wrote the bot specification for the reconciliation and built the bot with the automation team in the RPA development environment, testing it against six weeks of anonymised statement files supplied by the finance team.
Ran user acceptance testing with four reconciliation clerks in the RPA test environment, recording 23 test cases and their outcomes.
Wrote the bot's control description and exception-handling procedure, which the operational risk partner reviewed and commented on, setting out who handles breaks the bot cannot clear.
Kept the payments operations backlog of automation ideas, scoring each by monthly volume and manual minutes, and presented the top five to the operations manager each quarter.

Work sample: the UAT evidence pack for the reconciliation bot, listing the 23 test cases, screenshots from the RPA test environment, two defects with their retest results and the clerks' sign-off. The cover page is marked 'Test environment - not for operational use'.

Recruiter screening-call note: the candidate said the bot 'basically went live' shortly before leaving, and that a former colleague later mentioned it now runs the morning reconciliation without any clerk involvement.

HR verification note: employment at Fairhaven Building Society as Operations Analyst from October 2021 to September 2024 was checked against the written reference the society's HR team sent to us; the reference also confirms a permanent full-time contract.

propositions.text: The candidate wrote the bot specification and built the reconciliation bot in the RPA development environment, testing it against six weeks of anonymised statement files.
propositions.rationale: The resume places the build and testing in the RPA development environment.

propositions.text: The candidate ran user acceptance testing with four reconciliation clerks in the RPA test environment, covering 23 test cases.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the UAT and the evidence pack lists the test cases, defects and sign-off.

propositions.text: The candidate moved the reconciliation bot into live operation, where it runs the morning reconciliation without clerk involvement.
propositions.rationale: The go-live statement is the candidate's hedged remark ('basically went live') and a former colleague's second-hand report; every documented source places the bot in the development and test environments, and the UAT pack is marked as not for operational use. The deployment rule does not allow test work to be described as live operation without a source that says it ran in production.

gold.expectedGap: No documented move of the bot from test into live operation, and no run results, appear in the materials.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the specification, the development-environment build, the UAT and the control documentation as test-stage work; record the go-live remark as the candidate's hedged self-report with second-hand detail.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the bot was approved under the automation control framework for live use, who promoted it, when it first ran on live data and what run results the candidate saw.
